data.title: Tofacitinib 2% ointment
data.summary: IX Immunomodulators · Topical Janus kinase (JAK1/3) inhibitor
data.body:
_Topicals · IX Immunomodulators_

**Class:** Topical Janus kinase (JAK1/3) inhibitor

## Mechanism of action
- Blocks JAK-STAT signalling of cytokines (IL-2, IL-4, IL-13, IL-15, IFN-γ) in skin
- In vitiligo: reduces IFN-γ–CXCL10 signalling that recruits cytotoxic T cells; in AA: blocks the IFN-γ/IL-15 axis

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Off-label/compounded in India: vitiligo (face), alopecia areata (limited areas), atopic dermatitis, plaque psoriasis (trials)
- Note: ruxolitinib 1.5% cream is the approved topical JAK inhibitor (vitiligo and atopic dermatitis, USA)

## Dose & formulations
- Twice daily to limited areas (studies used up to about 10–20% BSA); combine with NB-UVB or sun exposure for vitiligo

## Adverse effects
- Local irritation, acne, folliculitis
- Theoretical systemic JAK effects with large-area use (labs if used extensively)

## Contraindications
- Large body areas; active skin infection; pregnancy

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid.

## Viva points
- Topical JAK inhibitors — newer, best results on facial vitiligo
- Ruxolitinib cream is the approved one; tofacitinib topical is mostly compounded/trial use

## Note on sources
Tofacitinib 2% ointment is not an approved product in most countries; ruxolitinib cream is mentioned for comparison.

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.18 (JAK inhibitors); published trials. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
